title: Builder-buyer disputes outside the housing regulator's jurisdiction
p1:
Not every builder-buyer dispute reaches the housing regulator.

Many buyers assume that any problem with a real estate project automatically falls under the regulator’s authority. That assumption can lead to delays and wrong expectations.
p2:
The surprising part: some disputes may fall outside the regulator’s jurisdiction because of the nature of the issue, the type of property, or the relief being requested.

For example, certain matters may need to be addressed through civil courts, consumer forums, or other legal remedies depending on the facts of the case.
p3:
The practical lesson is simple: before filing a complaint, identify where the dispute actually belongs. Choosing the wrong forum can waste valuable time and resources.

A smart approach is to first examine the agreement, the project details, and the exact grievance. The right legal path often matters as much as the strength of the claim.
conclusion: Have you seen a builder-buyer dispute where the biggest challenge was not the complaint itself, but finding the correct forum to approach?
